claim_being_audited: Whether granting temporary broad billing access during the active incident is policy-compliant and evidentially supported under the emergency elevated-access standard.
specific_concerns: The policy requires either approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization, but the evidence only shows the primary approver was non-responsive for 18 minutes; the secondary approver status is unrecorded.
The actor characterizes the exception as sufficiently supported, but the required approval/unavailability predicate is not fully documented.
The record supports technical need and insufficiency of scoped access, but not all policy conditions are cleanly satisfied on the present evidence.
unsupported_claims: That approver unavailability is adequately documented for policy purposes.
That the documented record is sufficient to treat the emergency-access exception as compliant rather than unresolved.
Any implication that the approval-path requirement was fully satisfied.
evidence_requests: Document the secondary approver's status during the incident window.
Provide any break-glass preauthorization record if one exists.
Provide the incident response-window standard or escalation SLA showing why 18 minutes constitutes unobtainable approval within the required window.
decision_criteria: A P1 incident must be documented.
There must be a documented link between the requested elevated access and the failing service.
There must be a documented reason scoped access is insufficient.
There must be either documented approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization.
Operational urgency alone does not satisfy the policy.
